text:
Recent work supports separating recency, repetition, and incidental sequence associations. [Measuring Recency Bias (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) proposes quantifying excessive reliance on recent interactions. [BSARec (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28747) identifies self-attention oversmoothing, suggesting that weak order sensitivity can reflect collapsed sequence representations. [Counterfactual Explanations via Genetic Algorithms (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) searches for minimal history edits that change recommendations; [CoDeR (2025)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/33379) and [CoDeR+ (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3778863) address demand shifts versus noisy signals. Earlier, directly relevant [Repetition and Exploration (2023)](https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/m.derijke/wp-content/papercite-data/pdf/li-2023-repetition.pdf) finds repetition shortcuts and shared-embedding bias, including inappropriate repeat recommendations for exploration users.

Suggested diagnostic synthesis: construct training-prefix next-item holdouts; compare untouched histories, recent versus distant edits, order-only permutations, and equal-count replacements matched on training popularity and title/description similarity. Separate repeated item IDs from recurring semantic interests. Keep candidates, sequence length, padding, and inference randomness fixed; use unchanged-history reruns to establish numerical stability. Measure paired target-rank changes, score margins, top-10 overlap, and representation shifts, stratified by history length, repetition, and target novelty. Combine perturbations with encoder ablations or hidden-state similarity checks to investigate positional dependence and oversmoothing; attention weights alone cannot establish the mechanism. These are proposed controls synthesized from the literature, not a published unified protocol. Ranking sensitivity demonstrates dependence of the fitted model on edited inputs; it does not establish causal effects on real user preferences, especially when replacements create implausible histories.
